claims.text: Under automated sync without selfHeal, a change made in the cluster (kubectl scale of the api to 4) makes the Application OutOfSync, Argo CD starts no sync, and the api keeps running with 4 replicas (observed after 30 s).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-self-heal.txt lines 1-3

claims.text: selfHeal and prune are boolean fields under spec.syncPolicy.automated of an Application; apps/staging.yaml sets both to true, staging-auto.yaml sets both to false.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup > Applications (application.yaml); apps/staging.yaml:22-25, staging-auto.yaml:21-24 @ stage-3

claims.text: With selfHeal: true, Argo CD also starts a sync when the live objects drift from Git, without a commit; the api returns to the 2 replicas Git declares shortly after kubectl scale (within the script's 120 s wait, no refresh asked).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; gitops-self-heal.sh:53-57 and output last line @ stage-3

claims.text: Argo CD keeps comparing live objects with the manifests in Git without anyone running a command, unlike OpenTofu (drift found only at plan). On its own it rereads Git every few minutes (polling) and follows live objects as they change (watch).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Architecture (application controller continuously monitors); Git Webhook Configuration (polls Git every three minutes); Reconcile Optimization / cluster cache; OpenTofu docs: plan

claims.text: By default a sync applies every object of the Application, not only changed files (ApplyOutOfSyncOnly applies only differing ones; neither staging Application sets syncOptions), so an unrelated commit's sync also resets the api to Git's replicas (output: 'after the sync of that commit: 2 replicas').
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Sync Options / Automated Sync Policy; gitops-self-heal.sh:26-35 and output line 6 @ stage-3

claims.text: Without prune: true, removing a manifest from the folder leaves its object running; the Application is OutOfSync and the resource is marked requiresPruning=true in .status.resources.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Pruning; gitops-self-heal.sh:36-43 and output lines 7-8 @ stage-3

claims.text: With prune off in the policy, no automated sync deletes an object whose manifest left Git, not even the one for that commit; it keeps running, marked requiring pruning. Without selfHeal, automated sync starts only for an OutOfSync caused by a new commit, not by a cluster change.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy (automated sync will not delete resources no longer in Git; changes to the live cluster do not trigger automated sync); gitops-self-heal.sh:36-43 @ stage-3

claims.text: With prune: true, a sync deletes an object whose manifest left the folder. After apps/staging.yaml is applied with no new commit, the still-OutOfSync Application (prune-demo) is enough, with selfHeal on, to start a sync that deletes it (NotFound, Synced).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Pruning, Automatic Self-Healing; gitops-self-heal.sh:50-52 and output lines 11-13 @ stage-3

claims.text: Prune and self-heal act only on objects that are part of the Application (came from its folder); other objects in the namespace donhang are not tracked by it and are left alone.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Resource Tracking; apps/staging.yaml:18-21 comment @ stage-3

claims.text: apps/staging.yaml is the Application 'staging' in namespace argocd: source envs/staging at targetRevision main of the Gitea config repository, destination namespace donhang; lines 1-3 say gitops-self-heal.sh and dr-drill.sh apply it.
envs/staging/api.yaml declares replicas: 2 for the api Deployment at stage-3.

gitops-self-heal.sh: 9-10 define replicas, sync_status; 12-24 staging-auto.yaml, scale 4, refresh, sleep 30; 26-35 commit prune-demo; 36-38 remove, push, refresh; 40-43 wait OutOfSync, print requiresPruning; 50-57 apps/staging.yaml, scale 4, wait ≤120 s for 2. Other helpers: lib/gitops.sh.
app_refresh annotates the Application with argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=normal, which asks Argo CD to reread Git and compare now; it does not sync.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/lib/gitops.sh:105-107; Argo CD docs: Application refresh annotation

claims.text: kubectl scale deployment api --replicas=4 changes the live Deployment's spec.replicas, not the manifest in Git. kubectl rollout status (script line 56) waits until the Deployment's rollout completes, i.e. its Pods are ready; it starts nothing.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: kubectl scale; kubectl rollout status; Deployments > Scaling a Deployment, Deployment status

claims.text: With self-heal on, a fix that must last (e.g. 4 api replicas) should be made as a commit to the config repository rather than with kubectl.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 3 and misconception 3; Argo CD docs: Automatic Self-Healing

claims.text: Leaving self-heal off is defensible when a team wants hand-made changes to stay visible as OutOfSync instead of being erased; the cost is a cluster that runs, for a while, what nobody committed.
claims.source_hint: Opposing view to misconception 3; Argo CD docs: Automatic Self-Healing (opt-in, off by default)
